title: Scenario 3: a phone and a PC on one port
task: 1/1/6 has a phone with a PC plugged into it. ClearPass does not know the phone and the phone has no supplicant, so it fails; the PC cannot even try, because the port takes one client. Make 1/1/6 a multi-domain port, give LLDP-MED phones a VOICE role through a device profile (voice VLAN 30 tagged, data VLAN 10 untagged), and get both devices on. This is the lab bench from 2026-09-28, and it has the same trap.
hints: `aaa authentication port-access auth-mode multi-domain` on 1/1/6: one voice device and one data device.
`port-access lldp-group LLDP-MED-ENDPOINTS`, `match vendor-oui 0012bb type 1`: the TIA OUI every LLDP-MED device sends in its capabilities TLV.
`port-access role VOICE`: `device-traffic-class voice`, `vlan trunk native 10`, `vlan trunk allowed 30`. Then a device profile PHONES with the group, the role and `enable`.
Phone still nowhere? A port-access port drops LLDP from a client that has not authenticated. `aaa authentication port-access allow-lldp-bpdu` on 1/1/6 lets the switch hear it.

lldp.desc: Lab SIP desk phone (LLDP-MED class III), fw 1.0

checks.desc: The phone is the voice device, by device profile
The PC is the data device, by 802.1X
The phone took VLAN 30 from LLDP-MED
